Australian-built target drone, formerly on a pole at the gate of the Jervis Bay Range Facility, then on loan to Australia Museum of Flight at Nowra in 2017-18 and donated to the HARS annexe at Parkes. Repainted in a later dayglo scheme; no constructor plate located.
Handed over to the Parkes Aviation Museum, a HARS annexe, on 19 April 2018; serves as a static display and a spares source for the HARS flying Orion A9-753.

Ex-RAAF Neptune used as a spares source in the restoration of A89-280, which replaced it as a gate guard in October 2012. Offered for disposal in 2015 and donated to HARS in February 2016 for display at Parkes.
Ex-RAAF Neptune, a training aid at RSTT Wagga Wagga and then in storage at Point Cook for the RAAF Museum; gifted to HARS in June 2018. Listed by one survey as an MR.5.

description: Ex-Polish Air Force Iskra jet trainer registered VH-ADG and carrying Polish number 816. The same airframe also appears in an Albion Park inventory; it is recorded here once only.

Ex-Royal Australian Navy Wessex, instructional airframe at HMAS Nirimba from 1987 and a training aid at RSTT Wagga from 1994; returned to the Fleet Air Arm Museum by road on 7 December 2015 and now with the HARS collection at Parkes.
